title: Fix attack vs combat turn-event mismatch across ThreatDetector, character-state.ts, and interrupts.py

sections.what: Fix the event-name mismatch where engine combat emits turn_events with action='combat' while ThreatDetector, _vitalsScene in character-state.ts, and engine/interrupts.py only scan for 'attack', and remove _vitalsScene's redundant third threat loop.
sections.why: engine/combat.py (lines 515-519, 576-580, 621-625) and routes/action_handlers.py (lines 1387, 1391) record combat turn events with action='combat'. However static/js/agent/threat-detector.ts (lines 50-55), static/js/agent/prompt-builder/character-state.ts (_vitalsScene, lines 389-407), and engine/interrupts.py (HOSTILE_ACTIONS, lines 42-48) check only 'attack'. As a result, live combat events never trigger ThreatDetector or interrupt checks at all, while _vitalsScene duplicates a third diverging threat scan.
sections.how:
1. Update static/js/agent/threat-detector.ts (lines 50-55) to recognize normalized hostile/violent turn-event actions ('combat', 'attack', 'disarm') via a shared predicate helper.
2. Replace the independent duplicate threat loop inside _vitalsScene (static/js/agent/prompt-builder/character-state.ts lines 389-407) with a call to ThreatDetector so prompt status and replan/react danger cues never disagree.
3. Add 'combat' (and 'disarm') to HOSTILE_ACTIONS in engine/interrupts.py (lines 42-48).
4. Add unit tests covering combat.py -> record_turn_event(..., 'combat', ...) triggering ThreatDetector, _vitalsScene, and interrupts.evaluate().
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest on tests covering engine/interrupts.py against combat.py record_turn_event('combat').\n2. Run npm run build:ts and node tools/unit/run.cjs asserting ThreatDetector and _vitalsScene agree when turnEvents contain action: 'combat'.

acceptance.text: Violence event detection recognizes 'combat', 'attack', and 'disarm' uniformly in ThreatDetector instead of checking only action === 'attack'.
character-state.ts _vitalsScene delegates to ThreatDetector rather than running a third independent threat scan.
engine/interrupts.py HOSTILE_ACTIONS includes 'combat' (and 'disarm') so background interrupt evaluation catches real engine combat events.
